home.previewTitle: A taste of what you will learn
home.previewBody: رَحِيْمٌ follows the pattern فَعِيْلٌ. Words on this pattern describe a quality that is lasting and part of who someone is — like عَلِيْمٌ (all-knowing) and عَظِيْمٌ (supreme).

credits.title: Credits
credits.intro: This site is built on the work of many people. Every verse and word of the Quran shown here comes from the verified sources below; none of it is typed by hand or read from the slides.

items.contentAuthor: All the course content on this site — the lessons and their explanations — is credited to Mr M.Arham Elqi.
items.course: The lessons follow an Urdu PowerPoint course on Quranic Arabic (521 slides). The original slides are shown with every lesson. The text lessons were written from these slides and are drafts until a teacher has checked them.
items.kfgqpc: The verses are shown in the Madinah Mushaf (Hafs) text of the King Fahd Glorious Quran Printing Complex, obtained through the Quran.com API. The text is never altered.
items.tanzil: Tanzil Quran Text (Uthmani), Copyright © 2007–2024 Tanzil Project, License: Creative Commons Attribution 3.0. Used as the reference text for search and for checking every verse.
items.quranCom: Word-by-word English and Urdu meanings, transliteration and word recitations, through the Quran.com API. One Urdu word meaning (25:68, word 17) is corrected on this site.
items.corpus: Roots, lemmas, parts of speech and word segments, from the Quranic Arabic Corpus by Kais Dukes (version 0.4, with corrections by mustafa0x), used under the GNU General Public License.
items.alafasy: Verse recitations by Mishary Rashid Alafasy (128 kbps), from EveryAyah.com.
items.hafsFont: KFGQPC Uthmanic Script Hafs font, by the King Fahd Glorious Quran Printing Complex.
items.otherFonts: Amiri, Noto Nastaliq Urdu and Inter, under the SIL Open Font License (from Google Fonts, hosted on this site).
items.software: Next.js, React, Tailwind CSS, Zustand, ts-fsrs (spaced repetition), Pagefind (search) and Phosphor Icons — all open-source.

credits.mistakes: Found a mistake? Please tell a teacher or the site owner. Corrections to lessons are welcome; the Quran text itself always comes from the sources above.
